newsitem.title: UK: Uk's Horlick returns heartened by bank talks.
newsitem.headline: Uk's Horlick returns heartened by bank talks.

text.p: Defiant fund manager Nicola Horlick returned to Britain on Friday after confronting her old bosses in Frankfurt, saying she still hoped to win back her high-powered job with a subsidiary of Deutsche Bank.
Horlick, former head of pension fund business at London-based Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), arrived at London's Heathrow airport declaring herself "very heartened" by the meeting.

But a spokesman for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said no concessions were made at the talks in Germany and the company had listened to her only as a courtesy. "No concessions were made at all," said spokesman Markus Will.

Horlick, 35, a high-flier reputed to have earned one million pounds ($1.67 million) a year, was suspended this week pending an internal investigation into what Deutsche Morgan Grenfell described as "a potential breach of her contract." She resigned on Thursday.
The dispute is believed to centre on allegations that Horlick tried to take some of her MGAM team with her in a move to Dutch Bank ABN AMRO.
After a two-hour meeting in Frankfurt that yielded no decision on her future, Horlick said she would seek an unspecified amount of compensation unless she was reinstated.

She said she was impressed by the attitude of the officials she met. No formal agreement was reached but she said Deutsche, parent of the fund management company, would now examine the allegations against her.

But the Deutsche Morgan Grenfell spokesman stressed that the talks were purely a courtesy and said Horlick had been told that any matter relating to her former employment with MGAM had to be addressed to the company in London.
Horlick, a mother of five who has been dubbed Superwoman by the British press for juggling family and career, said she planned to spend the weekend with her children.
